newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus eyes charters for Beluga freighter.
newsitem.headline: Airbus eyes charters for Beluga freighter.

text.p: Airbus Industrie said it was targeting the ad hoc cargo charter market with its Super Transporter A300-600ST (ST) freighter, nicknamed the "Beluga."

"The Super Transporter's primary role is in transporting sections of Airbus aircraft from factories in Europe to final assembly lines in Toulouse and Hamburg. However, we do see some scope for ad hoc charter flights in utilising spare capacity," Arnaud Martin, director of business development at Airbus Transport International, Airbus Industrie's airline subsidiary, told Reuters.
Airbus has two STs currently in service and plans to take delivery of a further two in April 1997 and June 1998.

According to Airbus data, the ST is the world's largest cargo aircraft in terms of volume, with a cargo bay 7.1 metres in diameter and over 39 metres long. It can carry loads of up to 45 tonnes over a distance of 1,670 kilometres.

"Because of capacity constraints, our ad hoc charter activity will only really begin with the arrival of our third ST and we expect it to account for around 20 percent of global flying hours undertaken by the aircraft, said Martin.
Each ST has a maximum capacity of 1,200 flying hours per year and each ad hoc flight will probably have an average duration of between five and six hours, he added.
The Beluga is the replacement for the Airbus' ageing fleet of Super Guppies, two of which are still in service but with significantly reduced capacity and are due to be phased-out in July 1997.
The Super Guppy, which began service in 1971, has a capacity of around 25 tonnes.

"While ST ad hoc charters will remain a sideline for us, we are seeking to develop a niche market for outsize, high value cargoes such as satellites, the larger airliner engines, helicopters and other bulky loads. Our main competitor is probably the Antonov AN124 which is tonnage rather than volume-orientated."
The ST made its maiden ad hoc charter late last month transporting a 40-tonne space station module from Toulouse to Turin.

The module, built by Italy's space agency, Alenia Spazio, was undergoing tests at the Centre National des Etudes Spatiales (CNES), in Toulouse. At end-1997, the ST is due to transport the same module to the Kennedy Space Centre in Florida for a space shuttle flight.

"We are in advanced negotiations with satellite manufacturers in Europe and the U.S. for other ad hoc charters while we also see some short-term potential in transporting chemical tanks," Martin added.

The ST is manufactured by the Special Aircraft Transport International Company (SATIC), a joint-venture company in which Airbus Industrie members Aerospatiale and Deutsche Aerospace Airbus each hold a 50 percent stake.

Other partners in the Airbus consortium are British Aerospace Plc, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA CASA of Spain. On December 6, Aerospatiale said Italy's Alenia would draw closer to the consortium without becoming a partner.
